report.title: Data and Schema Migration Readiness Assessment

handling.actualEgressStatement: Approved local public-repository metadata, selected source/document content and derived findings were processed in the active OpenAI Codex session. Assessment collection used no network provider, registry, scanner or remote GitHub/CI query. The user separately authorized commits and pushes of reviewed assessment artifacts to the existing origin remote.
redactions: No raw source excerpts, credential values, private overlays or author identities are included.
Evidence uses portable repository-relative paths; aggregate counts and team roles replace personal activity.

permissionsGaps.impact: The report is partial; missing evidence is not a pass and no numeric maturity score or delivery authorization is inferred.
permissionsGaps.summary: External consumers, accountable data ownership, availability/downtime targets, recovery objectives and migration requirements have not been supplied. No database, migration target or live data access is in scope.
Service region, retention/deletion and approval expiry are not supplied by local repository evidence.
permissionsGaps.impact: Owner governance details remain unknown; assessment findings await user review.

findings.title: Source-health rows are not unique by source identifier
findings.description: The source-health ledger contains 3,255 rows for 3,248 registered source IDs. Six IDs are duplicated, including one ID with three rows. The current repository validator reduces health rows to a dictionary keyed by ID before comparing coverage, so duplicates are overwritten and the validator still passes. This can distort aggregate reporting and makes duplicate records invisible to the main consistency gate.

remediation.summary: Canonicalize source-health output to one record per source ID and make duplicate IDs a schema or repository-validation failure.
steps: Choose and document whether source-health is a current snapshot or an append-only history; its current schema and consumers behave like a current snapshot.
Deduplicate the six affected IDs deterministically while preserving the intended latest observation.
Add an explicit duplicate-ID check before dictionary construction in the repository validator.
Add a regression test with duplicate rows and verify the validator fails with a precise diagnostic.

findings.title: Declared catalog schemas are not uniformly applied
findings.description: Only the source-freshness catalog is passed to validate_json_schema in main. The other schemas are parsed as JSON, while their catalogs rely on handwritten checks. Those checks cover many business rules but do not establish parity with every declared constraint, creating a compatibility gap when schemas evolve.

remediation.summary: Make schema-to-catalog validation explicit while retaining the cross-catalog business rules.
steps: Inventory each catalog/schema pair and its consumers.
Add negative contract cases for unknown properties, type changes and required fields before changing enforcement.
Verify declared schemas and handwritten invariants fail consistently; decide compatibility and historical-record handling before rollout.
